lookWhy: As leaves.json: the four atlas boards, emitted whole by Magerie (#1196, #1155). On SwiftShader oakLeaves and birchLeaves fail the cutout (123 and 187 pixels on 10 Nov 2026, where a GPU has 11 and 27): onejs-play issue 8 has what the pixels are and why the bound stays.

textures.lookWhy: The mass boards amplify float maths no node gets wrong. Fed Magerie's exact inputs (--chain with --isolate, floats unrounded), every node of both boards matches to 1/8192. Drawn whole, differences under that pass a Levels whose input window is 0.04 wide (gain 25), copied 900 times by Scatter, then a Gradient Map of hard bands 0.04 apart moves pixels at a band's edge by a band's colour (max 21). Measured on 9 Nov 2026: oak 2.8% of bytes off by > 2, birch 1.3%, mean 0.20 and 0.16. Each board has its own bound, its clean measurement plus a margin that a Warp drawn 5% too strong (--plant warp) still breaks: that plant measures 4.1% on this GPU and 4.2% on SwiftShader (clean 2.8% on both, 10 Nov 2026), so 4% holds oak; a bound shared with birch let the plant pass on birch.
